review_evidence: Verified both paths from the brief exist under port-sources/metamath__set.mm (a new nonstandard checkout-path prefix for this session).
Byte/line counts: set.mm 51,423,109 bytes / 880,268 lines; iset.mm 11,985,829 bytes / 221,748 lines.

Read the head (~2000 bytes) of both files: identifying `$( ... $)` header comments, CC0 public-domain dedication, and contributor lists -- set.mm created by Norman Megill in 1992, iset.mm forked from set.mm by Mario Carneiro in 2015 for intuitionistic logic.

Ran statement-count greps using Metamath's own documented syntax (` \$a ` for axiom/definition/syntax statements, ` \$p ` for theorem-with-proof statements, per the header comment at set.mm:188-189): set.mm 3097 `$a` / 47900 `$p`; iset.mm 916 `$a` / 16440 `$p`.

Read a full `$p` proof block sampled from mid-file in set.mm (theorems `2p2e4` and `2times`, around line 139064): each has a contributor-attribution comment, a formal prefix-notation statement, and an encoded compressed proof terminated `$.` -- a genuine checkable proof record.

Read the tail (~500-800 bytes) of both files: set.mm ends with a complete `young2d` $p proof block and properly nested mathbox/file-inclusion closing comments; iset.mm ends with a complete `alseu-no-surprise` $p proof block (dated 22-Jul-2026) and a proper mathbox-closing comment -- neither file is truncated or corrupted.
summary: Surveyed the checkout (metamath__set.mm, hydrated at port-sources/metamath__set.mm -- a third nonstandard checkout-path prefix seen this session, after reservoir-sources/ and the unprefixed MichaelStollBayreuth__LegendreQF case): confirmed both review-list files exist and are the two primary Metamath databases named by the prior review RRV-8f8eae168985-r1 ('the primary Metamath databases are rigorously checked formal statement/proof corpora and constitute the repository's mathematical content'). These are large plain-text .mm files (set.mm 51,423,109 bytes / 880,268 lines; iset.mm 11,985,829 bytes / 221,748 lines), too large to read byte-for-byte, so I surveyed head, a mid-file sample, and the tail of each, plus statement-count greps using Metamath's own syntax markers. Read the head of both files (first ~2000 bytes each): both open with a `$( ... $)` comment block identifying the file (set.mm 'Metamath source file for logic and set theory', created by Norman Megill 1992; iset.mm 'Metamath source file for intuitionistic logic and set theory', forked from set.mm by Mario Carneiro in 2015), state a CC0 public-domain dedication, and list dozens of named contributors -- consistent front matter for a genuine, actively maintained formal corpus, not a data dump. Ran statement-count greps for Metamath's `$a` (axiom/definition/syntax) and `$p` (theorem-with-proof) markers (` \$a ` / ` \$p ` with surrounding spaces, matching the syntax documented in the files' own header comments at set.mm:188-189): set.mm has 3097 `$a` statements and 47900 `$p` statements; iset.mm has 916 `$a` statements and 16440 `$p` statements -- tens of thousands of genuine, individually labelled formal theorems with encoded proofs in each file. Read a full `$p` block sampled from mid-file in set.mm (`2p2e4`, `2times`, around line 139064): each entry has a contributor-attribution comment, a formal statement in Metamath's prefix syntax, and a compressed proof (`$= ... $.`) -- a real, checkable proof record, not a placeholder. Read the tail of both files (last ~500-800 bytes): set.mm ends with a complete, well-formed `$p` proof block (`young2d`) followed by proper `$}`/`$(End of ... mathbox)$)`/`$( End $[ ... $] $)` closing comments, confirming the file is not truncated; iset.mm similarly ends with a complete `$p` block (`alseu-no-surprise`, dated 22-Jul-2026, i.e. actively maintained) followed by a proper mathbox-closing comment. Both files are genuine, complete, massive formal-proof databases -- exactly the primary mathematical content this corpus indexes. No exclusions.
